Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1359.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Ying'an Tanhua. Danxia Tianran owns the exact utterance inside Ying'an Tanhua's hall raising: visiting National Teacher Zhong asleep, and told by the attendant that though present he sees no guests and even the Buddha's eye would not see him, Danxia pronounces dragons give birth to dragon sons, phoenixes to phoenix young; the attendant reports it, the teacher strikes him twenty blows and expels him, and Danxia hearing of it says no mistake about the National Teacher of Nanyang.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T48/T48n2002A.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Rujing of Tiantong. Tiantong Rujing owns the retained deployment: at the fourth-month-eighth hall sermon he declares dragons give birth to dragons and phoenixes to phoenixes - pointing to heaven and earth, sole-honored - yet the rat raises its young along the roof beams; the assembly has seen through it, pours the dirty water over the head together, and ten thousand taels of gold are well spent.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1403.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tianru Weize. Tianru Weize owns the retained deployment: appraising Linji's sixty blows at Huangbo felt like wormwood twigs, he calls him a thick-skinned scabby-boned lout who knows no pain, unlike modern descendants with blood under the skin - what talk of dragons giving birth to dragons and phoenixes to phoenixes; even forcing open the golden palace lock and ringing the jade tower bell gets exposed by Chan master Duan and ends as dry clatter before the emperor.

Qianyan Yuanzhang owns the retained deployment: laughing at the raised Linji episode of wanting another beating - you are hurried in your own mind, the other will not be rushed; a real fellow would have tipped over the chan seat - he quotes the line the rats raise their young along the roof beams, dragons give birth to dragons and phoenixes to phoenixes, and notes Xinghua Cunjiang gained this one line from Linji and awakened to the purport of his master's blows at Huangbo at great Awakening's staff-tip.

Senses.Explanation: A lineage-and-kind image: the offspring manifests the family character from which it comes, commonly paired with dragons producing dragons. Liangshan Yuanguan uses the expression through active handling of Liangshan's answer about whose song and lineage he continues. Yuan'an Liao independently deploys it through independent direct deployment concerning inherited kind.
